chunk_findings.detail: The new filter only removes paths that are not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`; it does not apply the review's `exclude_globs`, so a tracked file the gate did not cover is still named. For example, if `snapshots/golden.json` is tracked and excluded from review via `[review].exclude_globs`, and it is the only file that differs between the base tree and the gate tree, `tracked` contains `snapshots/golden.json`, so `paths` still contains it and `_what_differs` names it. This leaves the reported “golden snapshots and transcripts” part of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files unfixed; the added regression test only asserts that `.merge_file_4zU3jH` is absent, not that an excluded tracked file is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_what_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The bug this change claims to close is two cases: merge temps tracked nowhere, and tracked files the review never covers (golden snapshots and transcripts matched by `[review].exclude_globs`). The new filter only drops paths absent from `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`. A tracked `snapshots/foo.golden` or `transcripts/run.json` that `exclude_globs` keeps out of the review is still in that set, so `_what_differs` still names it. Given a clean `HEAD`, a worktree whose only difference is that excluded golden file, and `own=None` (the call the new test uses), the note still contains the golden path, so the STALE mark still cannot be cleared by reviewing the covered code. The regression test never builds an excluded-but-tracked path, so it stays green while that half of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")` is the index-tracked set. A staged deletion (`git rm tracked.py`) removes `tracked.py` from the index, but `differing_paths` still returns it for the same base because the recorded worktree no longer has it. Since `tracked.py` is not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`, `_gate_covered` drops it, so the stale note does not name a deletion/rename even though the deleted file was tracked in the base and was a change the gate covered. Example: `git rm tracked.py`, then call `_what_differs(cwd, "HEAD", "clean", worktree_entries(cwd), ...)`; the only differing path, `tracked.py`, is filtered out, and the note omits the deletion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

evidence.note: Read the ask engine (services/ask/engine.py: QUESTION type has empty verb, answer() accepts free text via outcome 'answered' + text), the folded row (core/handlers/asks.py: verb str() default ''), and every approvals surface that filtered on verb (api/approvals.py _commands/approvals_show/_line, services/approvals/view.py waiting_for_a_person, api/approvals_harness.py approvals_ask, services/approvals/harness.py payload/attest). Confirmed: all of them drop question asks, so a question has no readable surface and engine.answer's free-text path has no caller.

r-approval-chat-channel (approvals surface through the operator's chat only); the question must be READABLE (show/list/pending) and ANSWERABLE in chat (harness ask payload is free text; attest records the free-text answer). A question is not approvable via the digest form (approve --all now skips it).

Committed 23b4babc9: removed the verb filters that dropped questions (waiting_for_a_person, _commands, approvals_show, approvals_ask); harness payload() emits a free-text question; attest() records the free-text answer (outcome 'answered') and verify() re-checks row.answer; approve --all skips questions. Regression test tests/test_question_ask_surfaces.py asserts show/pending/brief/list surface the question. Verified waiting_for_a_person + pending_line include a filed question.

Hunted the change for the six bug classes: the removed verb filters are pure row-field predicates, the harness payload/attest/verify branches on row.type==question (fail-closed: an unknown type stays an approval), approve --all skips questions explicitly. No off-by-one, empty-collection, dropped-config, torn-tail, unavailable-as-clean or dead-knob defect introduced.

No duplicated logic: the question branch reuses the existing engine.answer free-text path (outcome ANSWERED_WORD + text) and the existing harness scan/find/attest plumbing; approve/deny digest flow is untouched. No new helper duplicates an existing operation.

data.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:pipeline_by_diff

evidence.budget_forced: re-review the current tree: index-vs-worktree dirty scan (efa136405), missing import fixed, 4 findings confirmed+fixed 1 refuted

chunk_findings.detail:
An index-only staged logic edit to a path inside the committed trivial path list is invisible. `_uncommitted_not_in` deliberately permits dirty tracked files whose name is in `paths`, and `_is_format_or_comment` only runs `git diff HEAD -- :(literal)<path>`, which compares the worktree to HEAD and ignores the index. Concrete failure: base `foo.py` is `x = 1
`; HEAD changes it to `x=1
` (AST-equal/format-only), so `paths=["foo.py"]`. Now stage `foo.py` as `x = 2
` and then `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- foo.py`. `_uncommitted_not_in` sees `git diff HEAD --cached --name-only` output `foo.py`, but `foo.py in paths`, so it returns False. `_is_format_or_comment` sees an empty worktree-vs-HEAD diff and `_ast_unchanged` compares base vs HEAD (the format-only committed change), so `diff_is_trivial` returns True and skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`, even though a logic change is staged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: When the uncommitted-work guard fires (`tree is not None and _uncommitted_not_in(...)`), this function returns full `gates`, but it still returns `lambda: paths`, where `paths` is only the original committed `diff()` result. `ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py` later passes that same diff callable to `not_applicable`. In the exact case the guard exists for — committed diff is `README.md` and there is a dirty tracked `src/module.py` — `paths` remains `["README.md"]`, so any full-pipeline gate whose `applies_when` requires a Python path is marked not applicable and skipped. The guard therefore does not actually produce the full effective pipeline for the uncommitted dirty file; it should include the uncommitted paths in the returned diff when it forces `gates`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:pipeline_by_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The new call `diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, changed_paths(repo, it))` passes `cfg` in the position meant for the changed path list. The regression test pins `diff_is_trivial` as receiving the item and the path list as the first two arguments (`diff_is_trivial(None, docs_paths) == True`), with `cfg`/`repo` as the later context arguments. For a behavior-preserving docs-only change where `changed_paths(repo, it)` is `["README.md"]`, this call hands the config object to `diff_is_docs_only` instead of `["README.md"]`, so `diff_is_trivial` returns False; `_is_trivial` then returns False, and a large README-only diff falls through to `_selectable`'s size logic and still runs the whole suite instead of the new trivial scoped tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_is_trivial

chunk_findings.detail: A behavior change staged only in the index, on a path already in the committed diff, is still classified trivial. `_uncommitted_not_in` only fails closed when a dirty path is absent from `paths`, and `_is_format_or_comment` only runs `git diff HEAD` (worktree vs HEAD), not `git diff HEAD --cached`. Concrete case: commit a whitespace-only edit to `foo.py` (AST equal to base), then change `x = 1` to `x = 2`, `git add foo.py`, and `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree foo.py`. Worktree matches HEAD so the dirty check is empty, the path is in `paths` so the index-only name check does not trip, and `_ast_unchanged` compares base to HEAD and returns true. `diff_is_trivial` therefore skips rubber_duck, critic, and ci while the index holds a logic edit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: The new filter only removes paths that are not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`; it does not apply the review's `exclude_globs`, so a tracked file the gate did not cover is still named. For example, if `snapshots/golden.json` is tracked and excluded from review via `[review].exclude_globs`, and it is the only file that differs between the base tree and the gate tree, `tracked` contains `snapshots/golden.json`, so `paths` still contains it and `_what_differs` names it. This leaves the reported “golden snapshots and transcripts” part of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files unfixed; the added regression test only asserts that `.merge_file_4zU3jH` is absent, not that an excluded tracked file is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_what_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The bug this change claims to close is two cases: merge temps tracked nowhere, and tracked files the review never covers (golden snapshots and transcripts matched by `[review].exclude_globs`). The new filter only drops paths absent from `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`. A tracked `snapshots/foo.golden` or `transcripts/run.json` that `exclude_globs` keeps out of the review is still in that set, so `_what_differs` still names it. Given a clean `HEAD`, a worktree whose only difference is that excluded golden file, and `own=None` (the call the new test uses), the note still contains the golden path, so the STALE mark still cannot be cleared by reviewing the covered code. The regression test never builds an excluded-but-tracked path, so it stays green while that half of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")` is the index-tracked set. A staged deletion (`git rm tracked.py`) removes `tracked.py` from the index, but `differing_paths` still returns it for the same base because the recorded worktree no longer has it. Since `tracked.py` is not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`, `_gate_covered` drops it, so the stale note does not name a deletion/rename even though the deleted file was tracked in the base and was a change the gate covered. Example: `git rm tracked.py`, then call `_what_differs(cwd, "HEAD", "clean", worktree_entries(cwd), ...)`; the only differing path, `tracked.py`, is filtered out, and the note omits the deletion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

chunk_findings.detail: `_gate_covered` now filters `paths` through `then is None or p in then`, where `then` is the base commit tree. This drops every path that exists only in the current tree, including newly added tracked files. Example: base has only `a.py`; after `git add b.py`, `differing_paths(then, now)` returns `b.py`, but `b.py not in then`, so `_gate_covered` returns `[]` and the stale note omits the new tracked file. The previous filter `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")` kept such additions; it needed to be extended to also keep base-tracked deletions, not replaced with base-only membership. As written, a purely additive change in the gate's scope will not mark the gate stale, hiding unreviewed new code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

chunk_findings.detail: The index filter was replaced with `p in then`, and `then` is the reviewed base tree (`commit_tree_entries(cwd, base)`). `differing_paths` still yields additions, so a tracked file the gate would review that did not exist in the base is dropped before the exclude filter. Given a reviewed tree that has only `a.py`, then `git add b.py` (not excluded, not a merge temp): `differing_paths` returns `b.py`, `_gate_covered` returns `[]`, and the stale note stays empty even though the covered code changed. Staged deletions of base files are kept; newly added covered files are not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

chunk_findings.detail: For a question ask, `payload` returns an `AskUserQuestion` object with `"options": []`. Anthropic's `AskUserQuestion` tool requires each question to have 2–4 options, so `ddflow approvals ask <id>` for a question will produce an invalid tool input and no readable/answerable surface. That leaves the exact unreachable-question bug in place for the harness ask path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:payload (E.QUESTION branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The new brief text tells the operator to answer a pending question with `ddflow approvals ask ID`. That is not the answer route: an `ask` command asks a new question (and no `approvals ask` surface is part of this change; the free-text answer path is in `ddflow/api/approvals_answer.py`). For a pending question, `pending_line` will print the new guidance and direct the person to `ddflow approvals ask <id>` instead of the free-text answer command, so the question still has no usable answer surface from the brief. The new regression test only checks that the question id appears, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/view.py:pending_line

chunk_findings.detail: Question attestation records the wrong value and reads a field the write path never sets. Given a transcript answer "use postgres" for a question ask, the new branch sets outcome to E.ANSWERED_WORD and passes the person's text only as text=. E.answer is not modified in this change, and the bug states that free text is already accepted by engine.answer (the outcome direct callers pass), so this either raises TypeError on the unexpected text= keyword or stores "answered" instead of "use postgres". verify then requires h.answer == row.get("answer"), which stays unset when the reply was supplied as text=, so a question that was actually answered fails the level re-check and remains unreachable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:attest
